headline: Chelsea fined 150,000 pounds by FA over crowd misconduct in FA Cup tie with Charlton
facts: The FA said Chelsea were charged over supporters' conduct referring to religion or belief around the 56th minute of an FA Cup tie against Charlton Athletic.
Chelsea admitted the charge; an independent Regulatory Commission imposed a 150,000 pound fine, an action plan and a warning on future conduct.
Chelsea appealed, but an independent Appeal Board dismissed the appeal, so the original orders stand.
background: Chelsea are coached by Xabi Alonso this season, and the case concerns supporter behaviour at an FA Cup tie against Charlton Athletic.

headline: Ecuadorian player banned eight years for hitting assistant referee with a stone
facts: Perlaza, a 30-year-old midfielder, threw a stone from the bench area in the 96th minute on 17 October 2026 and hit the assistant referee in the face; the match was halted.
The official suffered a fractured cheekbone that needed surgery and was incapacitated for 60 days.
The federation's disciplinary commission banned Perlaza from all football activity for eight years, to 19 October 2034, and will ask FIFA to extend the ban worldwide.
The club was fined USD 2,000, must repay the referee's medical costs of USD 4,369.73 and must play three home games at a neutral venue; the club says he is no longer a member.
background: The case comes from Ecuador's third tier, where Yantzaza and Rio Aguarico played the match.

headline: Inquest into death of Sheffield United Women midfielder Maddy Cusack resumes in December
facts: The coroner's inquest into the death of 27-year-old Maddy Cusack is due to resume on 7 December for a five-day hearing in Derby, with 11 witnesses expected.
Her family made a written complaint to the club about her treatment under coach Jonathan Morgan; Morgan denies some of the claims.
The inquest was adjourned in July so the club could supply more evidence, including digital records and an audit of health records; an earlier start was postponed because of disclosure delays.
background: Cusack was found unresponsive at her home in Derbyshire on 20 September 2023 while a Sheffield United Women player.

headline: Southampton extend coach Tonda Eckert to 2029 despite Spygate fallout
facts: Southampton were thrown out of the 2026 Championship play-off final after admitting that a staff member spied on Middlesbrough's training; they were also docked four points this season.
The FA charged Eckert in July with three breaches of misconduct Rule E3.1; on 25 September he got a suspended six-week ban to the end of 2027/28, plus a fine.
On 20 November 2026 Eckert signed a new contract to 2029; owner Dragan Solak had backed him throughout.
Middlesbrough lost the play-off final 1-0 to Hull City on 23 May.
background: Eckert took full responsibility for the spying in June and said he had received police protection after threats.

headline: Oviedo fan gets suspended prison term for racist abuse of Kylian Mbappe
facts: A Spanish court gave an Oviedo fan an 11-month prison term for a hate crime, suspended on condition he stays out of stadiums hosting official competitions for two years.
The fan also received a financial fine; the amount was not given.
The abuse happened on 24 August 2025, when Real Madrid won 3-0 at Oviedo and Mbappe scored twice.
background: Mbappe joined Real Madrid from PSG in 2024, plays under Jose Mourinho this season and was a 2026 Ballon d'Or finalist, according to Sky Sports.

headline: Allegri banned two matches for abusing officials, then drops Napoli appeal
facts: Allegri was sent off after Napoli's 3-3 home draw with Roma, when he thought the late equaliser should have been disallowed.
He received a two-match touchline ban and a 10,000 euro fine, missing the games at Monza and Juventus.
Napoli first said they would appeal, but Allegri decided against it to focus on turning around a struggling league campaign.
He denied saying anything to the fourth official.
background: Allegri won multiple Serie A titles with Juventus and is known for touchline clashes with officials.

headline: UEFA fines England and hands suspended away-ticket ban over fans' chants in Madrid
facts: UEFA fined the FA 12,600 pounds and gave a one-match away ticket ban, suspended for a two-year probation, for 'racist and/or discriminatory behaviour'.
The cases came from England's 3-2 Nations League win over Spain in Madrid on 15 November.
Sky Sports News understands the punishment followed anti-Catholic and anti-Irish chanting; the FA said it will work with police to identify those responsible.
background: It was England's first visit to Madrid since 2004, when racist abuse was aimed at England's Black players, and Thomas Tuchel was angry that anti-racism protocol questions overshadowed the build-up.

headline: Premier League clubs vote 18-2 to cover legal costs of board members in Man City fallout
facts: On 19 November clubs voted 18-2 to indemnify five board members, including chair Alison Brittain and chief executive Richard Masters, if sued personally over possible defamation claims.
Manchester City and Nottingham Forest voted against; Forest said its vote was procedural and not support for City.
The vote follows the commission's September findings against City; Etihad is seeking legal advice and Etisalat called the findings false and defamatory.
City are appealing, saying the commission's opinion has material errors of law, principle and fact.
background: City were charged in February 2023 over more than 100 alleged breaches of Premier League financial rules, and the original hearing ran from September to December 2024.
footage_terms: Premier League chief executive Richard Masters

headline: Man City found guilty of breaking more than 100 Premier League financial rules
facts: An independent commission found City used sham sponsorship contracts between 2009/10 and 2017/18 to inflate revenue by 830 million pounds.
It also found misleading accounts, breaches of Premier League and UEFA spending limits, and a failure to cooperate; three of four cooperation-related charges were upheld and one was not proven.
No sanction has been set yet; a further hearing will decide it, with points deductions, fines, transfer bans or expulsion all possible.
City lodged an appeal on 1 October; the rules point to a decision around Christmas or January, and the club says it is innocent.
background: The period covered by the case is 2009/10 to 2017/18, and City were first charged in February 2023.
footage_terms: Manchester City verdict Premier League reaction

headline: Liverpool fan cleared after Antoine Semenyo withdraws support for racial-abuse prosecution
facts: A Liverpool fan was charged with racially aggravated behaviour over alleged abuse of Semenyo at Anfield on 15 August 2025, when Semenyo played for Bournemouth.
Semenyo was due to give evidence at Liverpool Magistrates' Court on 20 November 2026 but the prosecution said he was no longer supportive of proceedings.
The prosecution offered no evidence and the judge recorded a not-guilty verdict.
The trial had been adjourned in October when the defendant was taken to hospital after a seizure.
background: Semenyo left Bournemouth for Manchester City in January 2026.

headline: Infantino apologises to FIFA Council over abandoned World Cup stake sale
facts: At a three-hour Council meeting in Zurich on 15 October, Infantino apologised for not telling the Council sooner about a plan to sell a 20 percent stake in future FIFA tournaments to private investors.
The plan was dropped after strong opposition; the FA and UEFA still want him to resign, and UEFA wants all documents on the plan.
A FIFA Peace Prize given to Donald Trump in December 2025 is under review, with a decision due at the December 2026 Council meeting.
Infantino is seeking a fourth term at the March 2027 election in Morocco.
background: Infantino has led FIFA since 2016, and the Peace Prize to Trump has so far been its only award.

headline: Balogun's World Cup ban suspended after Trump call; FIFA to review disciplinary process
facts: The one-match ban on USA striker Folarin Balogun was suspended during the World Cup, after a call from Donald Trump to Infantino, according to Sky's report of the Council background.
Balogun played for the USA against Belgium while suspended; Sky raises questions about whether Trump or Infantino pressured the disciplinary committee.
FIFA's Legal Committee will review disciplinary procedures, with findings due at the December 2026 Council meeting.
The FA wrote to Infantino on 17 September about the World Cup sell-off plan and the Balogun controversy.
background: Balogun is a USA international whose move from Monaco to Everton collapsed on deadline day in September 2026.

headline: New York judge denies FIFA subsidiaries' bid to block UEFA evidence request over World Cup investor plan
facts: Judge Jeannette Vargas in the Southern District of New York denied motions by FIFA (Americas) Inc. and FWC2026 US, Inc. to intervene against UEFA's evidence request.
UEFA wants evidence about the FIFA Forward Enterprise plan from targets including Thrive, the investment firm of Joshua Kushner, and JP Morgan; no documents have yet been ordered.
UEFA filed in August as part of a wider effort to remove Infantino, including a possible criminal complaint in Switzerland.
ESPN reported on 19 November that UEFA also wrote to FIFA demanding documents about Infantino's role in the scheme.
background: The plan aimed to raise about 20 billion dollars by selling stakes in future World Cups and was dropped after a global backlash.
footage_terms: UEFA FIFA court New York Infantino

headline: FIFA chief legal and compliance officer Emilio Garcia Silvero steps down amid Infantino turmoil
facts: FIFA confirmed on 6 November that Garcia Silvero is leaving for a new professional chapter in Madrid after eight years in the role.
COO Kevin Lamour left in August and said the plan to sell a stake in World Cup commercial rights had 'deceived' FIFA's administration.
Arsene Wenger is reportedly not expected to renew his contract as chief of global football development.
Jan Kleiner will temporarily oversee the legal and compliance departments.
background: Garcia Silvero worked with Infantino at UEFA and followed him to FIFA, and also sits on the management board of the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

headline: Drone films 12 minutes of Pochettino's first Man United training session
facts: A drone operator filmed about 12 minutes of tactical drills at Carrington on 19 November, and reposts on X were viewed more than eight million times.
The operator apologised and removed the video, saying the flight was legal but filming the session was unethical.
United do not plan legal action now, as media were authorised to attend, but may act if it happens again; Goal says the club believes several laws were broken.
Liverpool coach Iraola said such filming should not be legal; the session came before United's trip to Anfield on 22 November.
background: Pochettino is in his first week as United head coach, and United have won one game in 11.

headline: Mudryk's podcast comments about his doping ban and Arsenal irritate Spurs fans
facts: On the Guest of Gordon podcast Mudryk discussed his drugs ban and how close he came to joining Arsenal in 2023, calling it his dream club.
Spurs fans were irked and Spurs were reportedly unaware of the appearance; De Zerbi defended him as a good person and player.
De Zerbi would not say whether the loan could be cancelled in January.
Mudryk is on loan from Chelsea, has played 16 minutes and is out with an ankle injury.
background: Mudryk moved to Chelsea in 2023 in the same window in which Arsenal were interested, according to ESPN.

headline: Wrexham fined 75,000 pounds by EFL for fielding two unregistered players
facts: The EFL fined Wrexham 75,000 pounds, of which 25,000 is suspended, for selecting two ineligible players this season.
Issa Kabore played in the 2-1 home loss to Birmingham on 28 August without his registration documents properly submitted.
Callum O'Hare was in the matchday squad as an unused substitute against Millwall on 2 September, but was not registered in time.
Wrexham reached an agreed decision with the EFL and said it is taking steps to prevent a repeat.
background: Wrexham are co-owned by Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney and are playing in the Championship.

headline: Neymar gets two-match ban for covering his mouth while confronting opponent
facts: Brazil's sports tribunal gave Neymar a two-match ban for covering his mouth with his hand while arguing with Bahia's Rodrigo Nestor, plus a third match for yellow cards.
The tribunal said he broke a protocol named after Vinicius Junior; Santos won the match 1-0.
Neymar and Santos can appeal the mouth-covering suspension.
background: The protocol was created after racism cases involving Vinicius Junior; Neymar returned to Santos in 2025.
footage_terms: Neymar reaction red card covering mouth

headline: Brazil court bans Internacional defender until injured Cruzeiro forward Gabriel Pec returns
facts: On 28 July 2026 Brazil's Superior Court of Sports Justice suspended Victor Gabriel until Pec is back in training, capped at 180 days.
His tackle on 22 July fractured Pec's left tibia, and he was charged with violent play under Article 254.
The ruling was split: one judge wanted a standard six-match ban, but three others backed the longer penalty.
Gabriel said he did not mean to injure Pec and apologised; the decision can be appealed.
background: Pec had just joined Cruzeiro from LA Galaxy in a club-record deal of at least 12 million dollars.

headline: Ex-San Diego FC striker Cedric Bakambu sues over alleged family-status housing discrimination
facts: Bakambu and his wife filed a federal lawsuit in the Southern District of California against property owners, Compass and two agents; MLS and San Diego FC are not named.
They allege discrimination because they have children, in a dispute about a pool barrier on a 17,500 dollars a month rental and a later Rancho Santa Fe offer.
Compass did not respond to ESPN; a Compass managing director allegedly said another applicant met requirements.
On 6 November Bakambu said on Instagram that he would no longer play for San Diego.
background: Bakambu is a former Villarreal and Marseille striker who joined San Diego FC in the MLS.

headline: Turkey arrests head of referee committee and deputy in refereeing probe
facts: On 29 September 2026 Turkish authorities arrested the head of football refereeing, his deputy and five others, after morning raids.
Justice Minister Akin Gurlek announced it; the probe covers alleged irregularities in ranking, assigning and scoring referees.
No formal charges were described.
background: Last year the Turkish federation suspended 149 referees and assistants over a betting scandal, and in July 17 club officials were detained in a betting and match-fixing probe.

headline: Haaland says Porto player grabbed his backside in ill-tempered Champions League clash
facts: Haaland scored both goals in City's 2-0 win at Porto on 8 September and says Rosario grabbed his backside in stoppage time; Haaland was booked after a scuffle.
Porto complained that Marc Guehi should have been sent off for arm-to-head contact on Gabri Veiga, and players clashed in the tunnel at half-time.
UEFA had announced no action; it will wait for referee and delegate reports before deciding.
background: Haaland joined City in 2022; he now plays under Enzo Maresca.

headline: Galatasaray and Fenerbahce players clash after Istanbul derby; coach promises punishment
facts: Galatasaray beat Fenerbahce 2-1 on 26 October at RAMS Park, with Osimhen scoring twice.
Players from both sides clashed on the pitch right after the final whistle; Archie Brown and Abdulkerim Bardakci were named.
Galatasaray coach Okan Buruk said penalties would follow, but no sanctions were reported.
background: Osimhen now has five goals in six appearances against Fenerbahce, with no defeats.

headline: Dani Alves ordered to pay Pumas 2.25 million dollars after Swiss court upholds CAS ruling
facts: The Swiss Federal Court confirmed on 11 June a CAS ruling that Alves must pay Pumas 2.25 million dollars, plus legal and procedural costs.
Pumas ended his contract in January 2023 after his arrest in Barcelona on a sexual abuse accusation.
A Spanish court overturned his sexual assault conviction in March 2025 after 14 months in jail.
CAS overturned FIFA's Football Tribunal in September 2025, which had ruled against Pumas.
background: Alves is 43 and became co-owner of Portuguese third-tier club Sporting Clube de Sao Joao de Ver earlier in 2026.

headline: Ronaldo retires from Portugal duty after row with coach Jorge Jesus
facts: Ronaldo, 41, announced on 5 November that he has ended his international career, with record totals of 146 goals and 243 caps.
He walked out of camp in late September after being an unused substitute in a 2-1 win over Norway on 27 September.
He said Jesus broke two promises; Jesus said the same rules apply to everyone and later admitted he mishandled the situation.
Ronaldo apologised to teammates and said the federation should decide any consequences; Portugal won their next two games without him.
background: Ronaldo's career has featured repeated rows with coaches at Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus.

headline: Maignan sent off at Bournemouth, then suffers racist abuse online; Milan condemn it
facts: Maignan was sent off in the 27th minute on 22 October for pushing Tyler Adams after putting gloves in his face; Bournemouth scored the penalty and won 3-0.
Milan called the online abuse that followed 'serious and unacceptable racist abuse' and backed Maignan.
The article mentions no investigation or UEFA action.
background: Maignan has spoken before about racist abuse, including walking off at Udinese in January 2024.

headline: Fenerbahce's Guendouzi banned two Champions League games after Lyon brawl
facts: UEFA banned Guendouzi for two Champions League games, including away at Aston Villa on 14 October, and fined him 50,000 euros.
The case came from the 26 August playoff at Lyon, where he made obscene gestures at Lyon fans and shouted pro-Marseille chants, sparking a mass brawl.
Lyon goalkeeper coach Antonio Ferreira got a three-game Europa League ban for kicking at Guendouzi; Mason Greenwood got a one-game ban deferred for a year, plus a fine.
background: Guendouzi is a former Marseille player, which is why the chants angered Lyon fans.
footage_terms: Lyon Fenerbahce Champions League playoff highlights

headline: Kyle Walker says he will not remove Man City tattoos, including '4 in a row'
facts: Walker posted that he has never had any intention of removing his City tattoos, which include '4 in a row' for City's titles from 2020-21 to 2023-24.
On talkSPORT he said he would probably have to remove them if City lost their titles, then said his post was meant to correct misleading headlines.
The talk follows the commission verdict against City, which is under appeal.
background: Walker won 15 major trophies, including six Premier League titles, at City between 2017 and 2025 and now plays for Burnley in the Championship.
